item.title: Okage Yokocho: Ise's Edo-Era Pilgrim Street — Guide
item.description: Stretching along the Isuzu River before the Naiku’s gate, Oharaimachi is the historic approach street to Ise Jingu, its stone-paved kilometre lined with traditional wooden merchant houses that have served pilgrims for centuries. At its heart is Okage Yokocho, a lovingly recreated quarter of Edo- and Meiji-era townscape packed with some 50 shops and eateries — a place to try soft Ise udon, grilled skewers, seafood and craft, and above all the famous Akafuku mochi, red-bean sweets served here since 1707.
